findings.title: A cross-site GET can change a logged-in user's notification preference
findings.body: `unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` on a GET endpoint, and this action is explicitly excluded from the XHR check. Since GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF verification, any third-party page can embed or navigate to `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` and silently alter the notification state of a visitor who is logged into the forum. The email link needs a user-specific, unguessable unsubscribe token (or a confirmation/CSRF-protected state-changing request after the GET) rather than authorizing the change solely with the ambient session cookie.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, leaving notification metadata and clients stale
findings.body: The action writes and saves the TopicUser record directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`, which is the normal notification-level update path. As a result it does not set `notifications_changed_at` or `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed`, and it does not publish the topic notification-level MessageBus event. A topic auto-watched due to a category can therefore continue to display its old automatic notification reason, and other open sessions/tabs for the user will not receive the state change.
